article.headline: Light Over Copper: A Photonics Pilgrimage for the Self-Reliant Retail Investor
article.lede: On X, a single well-followed account called Serenity has become something of an oracle for the AI-photonics trade — so much so that a fellow investor felt compelled to remind his followers they are, in fact, permitted to make their own investment decisions. The post lands somewhere between exasperation and affection, and raises a genuinely useful question: what exactly is the photonics thesis, and why has it proven so lucrative?
article.body:
The short answer is copper. The metal that has wired the world for a century is running out of road inside artificial-intelligence data centres, where the sheer volume of data moving between graphics processors — thousands of them bolted together in a single training cluster — exceeds what electrical signals can carry without melting themselves and the power budget simultaneously. The industry's answer is light: optical interconnects that use photons rather than electrons to shuttle information around at speeds copper cannot match. That transition, from pluggable transceivers to the more radical co-packaged optics (CPO, where the laser and the chip effectively share a housing), is the structural bet underlying what Serenity, whose X handle is @aleabitoreddit, mapped out under the heading of a "Photonics Supercycle."

The tweet from @Ren_aramb, posted in early May 2026, names the broad contours of that universe: SmartOptics (SMOP), Nokia (NOK), MaxLinear (MXL), Nynomic (M7U), Trio-Tech International (TRT), a Solana staking ETP (ASOL), and Lightwave Logic (LWLG) — alongside the benchmark outlier, Sivers Semiconductors (SIVE), the Stockholm-listed maker of indium phosphide lasers that had already gained more than 1,200 percent year-to-date by early May 2026. What the list reveals is that photonics is not a single product category but a supply chain — lasers, substrates, packaging, testing, modulators, transceivers — each populated by a small set of specialists.

Some of those specialists have earned their multiples. MaxLinear, whose infrastructure business grew 136 percent year-over-year in the first quarter of 2026, saw its share price triple in a single month after reporting that revenue from optical data-centre products was tracking toward $150–$170 million for the full year. Lightwave Logic, which makes electro-optic polymers (a material that converts electrical signals into light more efficiently than conventional silicon), soared roughly 344 percent in 2026 after a partnership with GlobalFoundries embedded its technology into a commercial silicon-photonics design kit used by data-centre chip designers. Nokia, not a name that sets retail hearts racing, quietly assembled one of the more complete optical portfolios in the industry through its Infinera acquisition, and launched a suite of AI-era coherent optics products in March 2026 capable of 2.4 terabits per second — the kind of throughput that NeoClouds, specialist AI computing providers that have sprung up to serve model trainers unwilling to wait for capacity from Amazon or Microsoft, urgently need.

The exception that proves the rule is POET Technologies, which Ren_aramb singles out with visible relish. POET builds optical engines — the compact modules that marry lasers and photonic integrated circuits — and spent much of early 2026 rallying on reports that Marvell Technology had integrated its components into AI hardware. When Marvell cancelled the purchase orders in late April, citing a confidentiality breach, POET's shares fell approximately 50 percent in a week. The episode illustrates the central risk in small-cap supply-chain investing: a single customer relationship can be the entire thesis, and customers defect. POET still has other orders and other partners, but the market penalised the concentration mercilessly.

The broader point @Ren_aramb is making is sociological as much as financial. Serenity's supply-chain analysis — which tracks chokepoints, the narrow nodes in a production chain where a single company controls critical flow — is genuinely sophisticated, and the public timestamped calls have been verifiable. But a methodology built on identifying overlooked monopolies loses much of its edge once the positions become common knowledge and the stocks have already tripled. The value of Serenity's thesis was in the early months of 2026, when few retail participants were mapping the indium phosphide substrate market or debating which laser die architecture would win inside a co-packaged optics module. By May, every photonics name in the basket carries a crowd.

That is the advice embedded in Ren_aramb's post, delivered with the equanimity of someone who has already found their own footing: follow the macro current — AI compute, the optical buildout, memory, NeoClouds — because the tailwind is real and durable, but do your own work on the specific names. Running someone else's thesis is comfortable until the moment it is not. A stock that goes up 500 percent because of a single influential account's conviction is equally capable of going down 50 percent when that conviction is tested, as POET's shareholders discovered in the span of five trading days.
article.fact_check: SIVE YTD gain of ~1,247% verified via stockanalysis.com and Yahoo Finance as of early May 2026. MXL infrastructure revenue +136% YoY confirmed by Q1 2026 earnings release. LWLG +344% in 2026 per stockanalysis.com. POET -~50% in one week confirmed by multiple outlets including Benzinga and Motley Fool following Marvell order cancellation. Nokia 2.4T coherent pluggable announcement March 16 2026 per Nokia newsroom. Serenity/aleabitoreddit profile corroborated by Singularity Research Fund substack article. M7U identified as Nynomic AG (German optical metrology). TRT identified as Trio-Tech International (semiconductor burn-in testing). SMOP identified as SmartOptics Group ASA (Norwegian optical networking). ASOL identified as 21Shares Solana Staking ETP — likely a different security than the photonics framing suggests; included as listed in the original post.
article.thread_summary: Ren_aramb encourages followers to invest independently rather than shadowing Serenity (@aleabitoreddit), noting that the photonics/AI/memory/NeoCloud macro thesis is broad enough that diligent investors can find their own names. Lists SMOP, NOK, MXL, M7U, TRT, ASOL, and LWLG as examples of stocks performing strongly, while singling out POET as the notable underperformer and SIVE as the extraordinary outlier (up ~500% in a month at time of writing). The tone is generative and pro-retail, not dismissive of Serenity.

ticker_smop.name: SmartOptics Group ASA
ticker_smop.blurb: SmartOptics is a Norwegian supplier of open optical networking hardware and software — transceivers, optical line systems, and management platforms — used by enterprises, governments, and telecoms carriers to build metro, regional, and data-centre interconnect networks. The company competes in the 'open optical' market where carriers avoid vendor lock-in by disaggregating optical hardware from the control plane. Founded 1990, headquartered in Oslo.
ticker_smop.recent: As of early May 2026, SMOP.OL was trading at approximately $6.03 (NOK equivalent), with a market capitalisation near $591M and trailing twelve-month revenue of $75.3M. The stock has been caught in the broader photonics sector re-rating driven by AI data-centre optical demand, though SmartOptics is more of an adjacent beneficiary — its open-networking solutions address metro and DCI (data-centre interconnect) use cases rather than the hyperscale co-packaged optics buildout at the centre of the AI optical thesis.

ticker_nok.name: Nokia Corporation
ticker_nok.blurb: Nokia is a Finnish telecommunications-equipment maker whose Network Infrastructure division designs optical networking hardware — coherent transceivers, optical line systems, and optical amplifiers — used by carriers and data-centre operators globally. The 2024 acquisition of Infinera, a specialist in coherent digital signal processing and indium phosphide photonic integrated circuits, gave Nokia one of the more vertically integrated optical stacks in the industry.
ticker_nok.recent: In March 2026, Nokia launched a suite of AI-era optical solutions including a 1.6T coherent pluggable for data-centre interconnect and a 2.4T pluggable for subsea and terrestrial transport, alongside four new digital signal processors built on both indium phosphide and silicon photonics. Nokia cited up to 70% total-cost-of-ownership savings versus prior-generation products. New line systems are expected in H2 2026; advanced coherent sampling begins mid-2027. At OFC 2026, Nokia emphasised that the Infinera acquisition provides the vertical integration needed to address the widening gap between AI compute and networking capacity.

ticker_mxl.name: MaxLinear, Inc.
ticker_mxl.blurb: MaxLinear designs mixed-signal semiconductors for broadband access, wired and wireless infrastructure, and — increasingly — optical data-centre connectivity. Its Keystone optical transceiver chip and Annapurna signal retimer are aimed at the 400G and 800G pluggable market serving hyperscalers and NeoClouds. The company pivoted aggressively toward AI optical infrastructure after years of relying on broadband and wireless revenue.
ticker_mxl.recent: MaxLinear reported Q1 2026 revenue of $137.2M (+43% YoY), with its infrastructure segment — primarily optical connectivity — growing 136% year-over-year. The stock surged approximately 80–84% in a single session on April 24, 2026, and gained nearly 200% across April. The company raised its full-year 2026 optical data-centre revenue guidance by $30–40M to a range of $150–170M, citing improved hyperscaler program visibility. Production ramps in optical products are expected to begin late 2026 and accelerate through 2027.

ticker_m7u.name: Nynomic AG
ticker_m7u.blurb: Nynomic (formerly known under earlier branding) is a German manufacturer of optical measurement and spectroscopy instruments used in industrial process control, agriculture, and medical diagnostics. It is not a photonics semiconductor company but rather an applied-optics instrumentation group — an adjacent beneficiary of the broader precision-optics and photonics supply chain rather than a direct player in AI data-centre optical interconnects.
ticker_m7u.recent: M7U appears in retail photonics watchlists as an adjacent beneficiary of the 2026 optical sector re-rating. Specific Q1 2026 financial data was not available in public search results at time of writing. The stock trades on the Frankfurt exchange; US retail access is typically via ADR or direct broker access to German equities. Coverage is thin in English-language financial media.

sources.title: M7U stock quote — Morningstar

ticker_trt.name: Trio-Tech International
ticker_trt.blurb: Trio-Tech International provides burn-in and reliability testing equipment and services for the back-end semiconductor manufacturing process. Burn-in testing stresses chips under elevated voltage and temperature to flush out early failures before they reach end users — a quality step used for memory, logic, and increasingly AI GPU silicon. The company also operates test service centres in Southeast Asia. It is an indirect beneficiary of AI infrastructure buildout through the semiconductor testing supply chain rather than a photonics company per se.
ticker_trt.recent: In March 2026, Trio-Tech secured a $5.3M order for burn-in boards for a next-generation AI GPU platform, signalling direct involvement in the GPU production supply chain. The stock gained approximately 421% over the trailing twelve months as of early May 2026, trading near $13.36. The gain reflects both the AI-hardware testing demand surge and the company's small-cap status, which magnifies price moves on modest volume increases.

ticker_asol.name: 21Shares Solana Staking ETP
ticker_asol.exchange: SIX Swiss Exchange / Euronext Amsterdam (ASOL.AS / ASOL.PA)
ticker_asol.blurb: ASOL is a European exchange-traded product (ETP) issued by 21Shares that provides physically-backed exposure to Solana (SOL), a proof-of-stake blockchain. The product passes staking yields to holders. It is not a photonics or semiconductor company. Its inclusion in @Ren_aramb's list alongside photonics names suggests it is being held as part of a broader AI/crypto/growth basket rather than a pure photonics play.
ticker_asol.recent: As of late April 2026, ASOL was trading near 57.06 (in ETP units), with approximately $1.45B in assets under management. Solana has benefited from sustained institutional interest in proof-of-stake networks and the broader crypto risk-on environment of 2025–2026. Coverage note: this is a European ETP, not a US-listed equity.

ticker_lwlg.name: Lightwave Logic, Inc.
ticker_lwlg.blurb: Lightwave Logic develops and licenses electro-optic (EO) polymer materials — branded Perkinamine — that convert electrical signals into light with greater efficiency and bandwidth than conventional lithium niobate or silicon photonics modulators. EO polymers can operate at higher speeds and lower drive voltages, enabling smaller, lower-power optical modulators for 200G and 400G per-lane data-centre and AI networking applications. The company does not manufacture transceivers; it licenses its material technology to foundries and systems integrators.
ticker_lwlg.recent: In April 2026, Lightwave Logic's polymers were embedded into GlobalFoundries' silicon-photonics platform via the GDSFactory design kit, targeting 200G/400G per lane data-centre AI applications — a significant commercialisation milestone. Shares gained approximately 344% in 2026 and reached a four-year high. A Motley Fool report noted insider selling of 20,000 shares in April 2026 following the run-up. The company ended 2025 with $69M cash, minimal revenue ($236,855 in FY2025), and an operating loss of approximately $20M — it remains pre-commercial revenue stage, funding operations from its cash balance.

ticker_sive.name: Sivers Semiconductors AB (publ)
ticker_sive.blurb: Sivers designs and manufactures indium phosphide (InP) distributed feedback lasers and optical amplifiers used inside high-speed optical transceivers, automotive LiDAR systems and satellite communications terminals. Its photonics business is one of the few independent western sources of the laser dies that go into AI-data-centre optical links, alongside larger incumbents such as Coherent and Lumentum. A separate wireless unit supplies 5G millimetre-wave RF chips. The company has been preparing a spin-off and potential dual Nasdaq New York listing of its photonics subsidiary.
ticker_sive.recent: Shares ran from roughly SEK 4 at the start of 2026 to a close of SEK 55.95 in early May, a year-to-date gain of about 1,247%, on customer wins including a 1.6T linear-drive optical module collaboration with Jabil announced 15 April 2026 and a LiDAR ramp scheduled for Q4 2026 with up to $138m of cumulative lifetime revenue. 2025 net sales were SEK 304m (+25% YoY) but the after-tax loss was SEK 186m, prompting an April 2026 directed issue of 8.62m shares at SEK 14.50 raising about SEK 125m at roughly 2.5% dilution. Photonics experts and Swedish business media have publicly questioned whether the rally has run ahead of fundamentals.

ticker_poet.name: POET Technologies Inc.
ticker_poet.blurb: POET Technologies develops optical engines — compact co-packaged modules that integrate lasers and photonic integrated circuits — targeting 400G, 800G, and 1.6T AI data-centre interconnect applications. Its POET Infinity platform is designed to allow customers to assemble high-density optical transceiver modules without owning their own photonics fabrication. The company raised approximately $375M in equity in Q4 2025 and carries roughly $430M in cash.
ticker_poet.recent: POET experienced one of the more dramatic volatility events in the photonics sector during April 2026. Shares rallied roughly 108% on reports its technology was being integrated into Marvell Technology's AI hardware stack via Celestial AI (which Marvell had acquired). On April 27, 2026, POET disclosed it had received notice of order cancellation from Marvell on April 23, with Marvell citing a confidentiality violation; shares fell approximately 50% in a single week. POET countered with a separate $5M production order for Infinity engines targeting 30,000+ units in 2026, and maintained partnerships with LITEON and Lessengers for 1.6T modules. The episode became a widely-cited example of single-customer concentration risk in small-cap photonics. @Ren_aramb's post singles out POET as the notable exception in an otherwise rising sector.
